chapter: Open sets, touring and Sweet Basil
title: Road work: Chico Freeman, abroad and one-off hires
summary: Freeman says he mostly toured alone, hired by agencies, and with Chico at Ronnie Scott's.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Who else did you go on the road with, as far as road stuff?
Mostly I’ve been out there with myself.
With a group that you put together.
Or one of these booking agencies put together, because I was always – the guy would say, “As long as you going to be there, we don’t care who you bring.”
When did the road stuff stop?

That must be George. Somebody with a key, right? I had mentioned that I had been out with Milt Trenier for about four years. And of course I traveled with Chico all over the world for two or three years.
But that’s recent. That was since the ’80s or something like that.
Really. Well, it started in ’79 and went to about ’85 maybe.
Actually, I was always going out and playing, like when I went out with you, for example, for a couple of evenings. I came right straight back home, and . . .
So it would be just these isolated hits.

. . . and you kept going. Everybody was using me that way, called me. So I was gone a lot, but it wasn’t with any group of mine. Whenever I played Paris, they always would hire the band. So I said, “Why don’t you let me bring a band?” They said, “You’re the kind of cat that can just work with anybody.” I guess all these years and all these sets . . .
In other words, they didn’t want to spend the money.
Yeah, well now you know I know that’s why they were doing that. Because when I went to England and worked . . .
. . . Ronnie’s, that was with Chico’s band.
